driver: Events counted per unit are recorded by instruments that keep their own drifting time and only their last few hundred records, read on an observer's schedule, so the units with the most events lose the most and line up the worst with the independent record that classifies them; the expected count each unit should have is learned only from unit-periods that a later physical check confirmed sound, and the alarm threshold carries the spread those confirmed units show beyond chance.
driver_concrete: Each zone's lightning faults are its reclosers' trips matched to located strokes on each controller's own clock (the radio-less controllers drift minutes between site visits and keep only their last 64 or 100 events, so a failing zone's busiest months are overwritten); the faults a zone would have with sound protection come from seasons the next cyclic inspection found sound, and the referral threshold carries the scatter of those confirmed-sound zones at no more than one sound zone referred a season.
stump: A careful run that matches the radio-less controllers' trips to strokes on a wide window around their own stamps, counts only the events their memories kept and fits the sound-protection rate on every season no inspection has yet found failed refers 2 zones against 15: the baseline holds the failing zones it should judge, the wide window counts storm trips as lightning and the lost and unread months are missing, so the season totals, the radio-less faults, the failed-protection faults, the alert load, the inspection check and the avoided faults are all off, each by a different route.
results: R1 the network's lightning faults per season, reconstructed on every protective device's own clock; R2 the radio-less zones' 2026 lightning faults with what their memories lost and their unread months filled; R3 2026's lightning faults failed protection caused (the season against every zone sound); R4 the zones the rule refers for the 2027 refit; R5 its referrals after each season since 2022; R6 the sound zones it should refer in a season; R7 its referrals against the following cyclic inspections (referred, confirmed, missed); R8 the lightning faults the refit avoids in a season of average lightning
one_fact_test: 'the reclosers with no radio link keep their own drifting clocks and only their last events between site visits' rescues R1 and R2; 'a season counts as sound only when the next cyclic inspection found nothing' rescues R6 and R8 (2 of 8 each)

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what restoring a unit's condition removes from its next-period event count, which is only the part of its event rate that has grown since the condition was last restored, per unit of an exposure that drives every event; the latest counts mix that growth with each unit's own base and with an exposure that moved in opposite directions across areas, so the units that look worst were selected on a high-exposure year or on a high base the restoration cannot touch, and the units with the most to gain look ordinary.
lineage.architecture: v1 (Kotuku Networks, the 2027 vegetation catch-up on six 11 kV feeders, one Poisson fit of tree interruptions on station gust load with growth since trim)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-11 before upload: cut under the retired single-deep-step design (READY 2026-11-09, never run on the platform); re-rooted at the author's word for a stronger chain with at least three independent analytical failure points. Its record: the storm-track swing between stations was thin (one plot of gust hours by station shows it), the plantation feeders' dense corridor sat only in the deciding units with one filter as the fix (a send-back), and every graded figure came out of one Poisson fit (one thing under another name).

differentiation.task13: v2 is a new world (a Philippine cooperative's lightning protection, not a New Zealand lines company's vegetation), a new answer shape (a monitoring rule with its alert load, not a ranked list) and a chain of eight results; nothing of v1's gust-load fit or trim-growth split survives
differentiation.mark196: mark196 recovers how many events a partly captured record misses from the overlap of two capture channels; here the events are recovered from one device's own record (a sequence gap and an unread tail) and its drifting clock against a lightning extract, and the decisive call is a referral threshold carried on the spread of inspection-confirmed sound units
differentiation.task6: task6 weights spans by a sampling share set where each trace starts and dates incident causes by onset; here no sample is drawn: events are aligned to an independent record across drifting device clocks, an overwritten memory is filled, and units are referred against a baseline confirmed by physical inspection
